Privacy Policy

Last updated: January 2026

Aiclona is a retrieval-augmented generation platform built for private, local-first knowledge workflows. This Privacy Policy explains how Aiclona handles the documents, knowledge bases, chat history, and configuration data that pass through your deployment, and describes the limited information collected through this portal page.

1. Scope of This Policy

This policy applies to (a) information you submit through the contact and inquiry forms on this portal, and (b) data processed by the self-hosted Aiclona instance you deploy from this page. Aiclona is designed to run entirely within your own infrastructure, and by default no document content, embeddings, or query history is transmitted to Aiclona maintainers.

2. Data Processed Inside Your Aiclona Deployment

When you use Aiclona to build knowledge bases and run retrieval or chat workflows, the following categories of data are processed and stored locally on the infrastructure you control:

  • Source documents you upload, including PDFs, Word, PowerPoint, spreadsheets, images processed through OCR, and web content you import.
  • Parsed chunks, layout metadata, tables, and structured elements extracted by the deep document understanding pipeline.
  • Vector embeddings and full-text indexes generated by the configured embedding models and search backend.
  • Chat sessions, prompts, retrieved citations, agent traces, and workflow execution logs.
  • Knowledge base configuration, chunking parameters, prompt templates, API keys for external model providers, and user account information for tenants of your deployment.

All of the above remains inside your database, object storage, and vector store. Aiclona does not phone home with document content, embeddings, or user queries.

3. Information Submitted Through This Portal

If you contact us through this page, we process only the details you provide (such as name, email address, organization, and message content) for the purpose of responding to your inquiry, providing deployment assistance, and following up on requested services. This information is not used for advertising or sold to third parties.

4. Third-Party Model and Storage Providers

Aiclona can be configured to connect to external services, including large language model APIs, embedding providers, rerankers, object storage, and vector databases. When you enable such an integration, prompts, retrieved passages, or embeddings are transmitted to the provider you selected under that provider's own terms and privacy practices. You are responsible for reviewing and accepting those terms, and for choosing local or self-hosted alternatives where required by your compliance posture.

5. Security and Access Controls

Because Aiclona is deployed within your environment, the security of stored documents, indexes, and credentials depends on the controls you apply at the network, operating system, container, and database layers. We recommend enabling authentication, restricting administrative endpoints, rotating API keys used for external model providers, and encrypting storage volumes that hold ingested content.

6. Data Retention and Deletion

Documents, chunks, embeddings, and chat history persist in your Aiclona deployment until you remove them. Deleting a knowledge base, dataset, or conversation from the Aiclona interface removes the associated records from the underlying stores you configured. Inquiries submitted to this portal are retained only as long as needed to complete the requested follow-up.

7. Your Rights

You retain full ownership of the documents and derived data inside your Aiclona deployment. For any personal information you have submitted through this portal, you may request access, correction, or deletion by contacting us at the address below.

8. Updates to This Policy

We may revise this Privacy Policy to reflect changes in Aiclona features, integrations, or applicable regulations. Material changes will be reflected on this page along with an updated revision date.

9. Contact

Questions about this Privacy Policy or about the handling of data by your Aiclona deployment can be sent to service@aiclona.com.

Cookie Policy

Last updated: August 2026

This Cookie Policy explains how Aiclona uses cookies and similar local-storage technologies on this portal page. It should be read together with the Privacy Policy. By continuing to browse this site, you agree to the use of the cookies described below.

1. What Are Cookies

Cookies are small text files placed on your device by a website you visit. Similar technologies include local storage, session storage, and pixel tags. Together they allow a site to remember your actions and preferences (such as language, theme, and login state) over a period of time.

2. Categories We Use

  • Strictly necessary — required for the site to function, including session identifiers, security tokens, and load-balancer routing. These cannot be turned off.
  • Preference — remember non-critical choices such as language and theme so the interface stays consistent across visits.
  • Analytics — aggregate, non-identifying page-view and performance data used to improve navigation and content. Enabled only after consent where required by law.
  • Marketing — currently not used on this portal. If introduced in the future, they will be listed here and gated behind explicit consent.

3. Third-Party Cookies

Some pages may embed content from third parties (for example, video or code-snippet providers) that set their own cookies under their own privacy policies. We do not control those cookies and encourage you to review the relevant provider's policy before enabling them.

4. Managing Your Choices

Most browsers let you view, delete, or block cookies through their settings. Blocking strictly necessary cookies may prevent parts of the portal from working. Where a consent banner is presented, you may adjust your preferences at any time via the "Cookie preferences" link in the footer.

5. Retention

Session cookies are cleared when you close the browser. Persistent cookies expire after the period stated in the cookie itself, typically no longer than twelve (12) months, after which consent is requested again where required.

6. Updates to This Policy

We may update this Cookie Policy when we change the cookies we use or when regulations change. The revision date at the top of this section reflects the most recent update.

7. Contact

Questions about this Cookie Policy can be sent to service@aiclona.com.

The Processor processes personal data solely to (a) provide, secure, and support the subscribed services, (b) fulfil billing and account management obligations, and (c) comply with legal obligations. The Processor processes personal data only on documented instructions from the Controller, including the acceptance of the Terms of Service and configuration choices made in the account settings. 4. Confidentiality

5. Security Measures

The Processor implements appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data, including encryption in transit, access controls, least-privilege administration, logging, vulnerability management, backup, and incident-response procedures. The Processor will provide reasonable prior notice of intended additions or replacements and will allow the Controller to object on reasonable data-protection grounds.

7. International Transfers

Where personal data is transferred outside the Controller's jurisdiction, the Processor relies on lawful transfer mechanisms such as Standard Contractual Clauses, adequacy decisions, or other approved safeguards, and applies supplementary measures where required.

8. Data Subject Rights

Taking into account the nature of the processing, the Processor assists the Controller by appropriate technical and organizational measures in fulfilling its obligation to respond to requests for exercising data-subject rights, including access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, and objection.

9. Incident Notification

The Processor notifies the Controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal-data breach affecting the services, providing the information reasonably needed for the Controller to fulfil its own notification obligations.

10. Audit

The Controller may audit the Processor's compliance with this DPA once per year, at the Controller's expense, on reasonable prior notice, subject to reasonable confidentiality and security constraints. Third-party audit reports may be provided in lieu of on-site audits where available.

11. Return or Deletion

Upon termination of the services, and at the Controller's choice, the Processor deletes or returns personal data processed on the Controller's behalf, except to the extent retention is required by law. Personal data stored inside the Controller's self-hosted Aiclona deployment remains under the Controller's control and is not affected by this section.

12. Liability

Each party's liability under this DPA is subject to the limitations set out in the Terms of Service or applicable order form. Nothing in this DPA excludes liability that cannot be limited under applicable law.

13. Contact

To execute this DPA or request the current sub-processor list, please contact service@aiclona.com.

Service Level Agreement

Last updated: August 2026

This Service Level Agreement (SLA) describes the availability commitment and service-credit remedy for paid Aiclona subscription plans purchased through this portal. It applies only to portal-hosted services (for example, the subscription management portal and any centrally hosted premium components), not to Aiclona software running inside the Controller's own infrastructure.

1. Definitions

  • Monthly Uptime Percentage — total minutes in a calendar month minus Downtime, divided by total minutes in the month.
  • Downtime — sustained periods during which the covered portal-hosted service is unavailable to the Customer for reasons attributable to us, as measured by our monitoring systems.
  • Excluded Downtime — see Section 4.

2. Availability Commitment

We commit to a Monthly Uptime Percentage of at least 99.5% for covered portal-hosted services.

3. Service Credits

If we fail to meet the commitment in a given calendar month, the Customer may claim a service credit against the affected plan's monthly fee:

  • Uptime < 99.5% and ≥ 99.0% — 10% credit
  • Uptime < 99.0% and ≥ 95.0% — 25% credit
  • Uptime < 95.0% — 50% credit

Service credits are the Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for availability shortfalls. Credits do not exceed the amount actually paid for the affected month and are applied to future invoices; they are not paid out in cash.

4. Exclusions

The following are excluded from Downtime calculations:

  • Scheduled maintenance announced at least 48 hours in advance, or emergency maintenance to address security or integrity risks.
  • Force majeure events, including natural disasters, war, civil unrest, and internet-backbone outages.
  • Failures of third-party model, embedding, storage, or infrastructure providers connected to the Customer's own deployment.
  • Issues caused by the Customer's software, hardware, network, misconfiguration, or violation of the Acceptable Use Policy.
  • Suspension resulting from non-payment, security investigation, or lawful request.

5. Claim Procedure

To claim a service credit, the Customer must submit a written request to service@aiclona.com within thirty (30) calendar days of the end of the affected month. The request must include the plan name, the affected dates and times, a description of the impact, and any supporting evidence. Approved credits are applied to the next invoice.

6. Maintenance Windows

We may schedule maintenance during low-traffic windows and will publish upcoming windows on the portal status area or by email. Emergency maintenance may be performed at any time to address a critical security or integrity issue.

7. Changes to This SLA

We may revise this SLA to reflect changes in service architecture or supported components. The revised SLA applies to renewals and new purchases made after the revision date; existing paid cycles remain governed by the version in effect at the time of purchase.

8. Contact

Questions about this SLA can be sent to service@aiclona.com.

AI Disclaimer

Last updated: August 2026

Aiclona uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), large language models (LLMs), embeddings, and related AI techniques to answer questions from your knowledge bases. This AI Disclaimer explains the inherent limitations of those techniques and your responsibilities when relying on their output.

1. Outputs May Be Incorrect

AI-generated outputs — including summaries, extracted answers, citations, tables, code, and translations — can be incomplete, out of date, biased, or entirely fabricated (commonly called "hallucinations"). Retrieval steps can also miss or misrank relevant passages. You are responsible for reviewing outputs before relying on them for consequential decisions.

2. No Professional Advice

Aiclona outputs do not constitute medical, legal, financial, tax, safety, engineering, or other professional advice, and are not a substitute for consultation with a qualified professional. Do not rely on Aiclona to make decisions that require professional judgement without independent verification by a suitably qualified human.

3. Human Oversight

You are expected to keep meaningful human oversight over AI-generated content, especially where the content will be used to (a) make automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effect on individuals, (b) support safety-critical processes, or (c) be published or distributed as authoritative material.

4. Third-Party Model Behaviour

When Aiclona is configured to use third-party model providers, output quality, latency, availability, safety filtering, and data handling depend on the selected provider. We do not control and are not responsible for the behaviour of third-party models; changes on the provider's side may alter outputs without notice.

5. Bias and Sensitive Topics

Language models can reflect biases present in their training data. Use appropriate caution when generating content about protected characteristics, minority groups, or contested topics, and apply your own review process before publishing such content.

6. Confidentiality of Prompts

Prompts, retrieved passages, and generated outputs may be transmitted to configured third-party providers. Do not include information you are not entitled to share with those providers, and configure retention and logging settings on both sides in a way consistent with your confidentiality obligations.

7. Reserved Behaviours

Aiclona may decline to answer, provide safety warnings, or apply guardrails on certain categories of requests. These behaviours are provided on a best-effort basis and should not be relied upon as a substitute for your own safety review.

8. No Warranty on Outputs

To the maximum extent permitted by law, AI-generated outputs are provided "as is" without warranty of accuracy, fitness for a particular purpose, or non-infringement, in accordance with the Terms of Service.

9. Contact

Questions about this AI Disclaimer can be sent to service@aiclona.com.
